roadmap.title: internal monologue intro
beats: I wake up screaming—not from pain, but from the sheer indignity of being swaddled like a sacrificial lamb.
The Hero King coos at me, and I realize with horror that I’m a baby, and worse, his baby.

roadmap.title: chapter 2
beats: I attempt to cast a simple dark scrying spell at four years old, but my mana backlashes, leaving me with a nosebleed and a week-long fever.
The court assumes I’m just "delicate."

roadmap.title: family interaction misunderstanding
beats: I draw a precise summoning circle with crayons, hoping to call a demonic gnat.
My mother finds it, tears up at the "family portrait" inside, and frames it.
I scream internally.

roadmap.title: chapter 4
beats: I manipulate the nursery maids into giving me extra dessert by saying, "Father says I’m his brave little soldier." It works.
I hate that it works.

roadmap.title: chapter 5
beats: My first tutor quits after I correct his spell formula mid-lesson.
The court assumes I’m a prodigy.
I am, but not in the way they think.

roadmap.title: chapter 6
beats: I attempt to "garden" a mana-siphoning crystal array in the royal gardens.
My father proudly shows it off as "Lily’s pretty rock garden" at a diplomatic summit.

roadmap.title: first scheme attempt
beats: I try to intimidate Prince Leo with a faint hex, but it feels like a tickle.
He thinks I’m flirting and challenges me to an arm-wrestling match.
I lose.

roadmap.title: comedic failure
beats: Leo "accidentally" throws me into a pile of hay during training.
The court gasps at his "playful strength." I plot his demise while blushing.

roadmap.title: chapter 9
beats: Eris arrives to tutor me in magic.
I correct her on a "lost" theorem, and she becomes my sobbing, obsessive fan.
I exploit this to get forbidden grimoires.

roadmap.title: chapter 10
beats: Zephyr visits and notices my dolls arranged in military formations.
He launches an investigation.
I feed his spies false leads about a "Crumble Conspiracy."

roadmap.title: chapter 11
beats: The "Crumble Conspiracy" report is presented to my father.
He laughs for an hour.
Zephyr’s reputation is ruined.

roadmap.title: emotional conflict hint
beats: I overhear my parents arguing about my "fragility." My mother suggests I might be "too advanced" for my age.
My father insists I’m perfect.
I feel something unfamiliar: guilt.

roadmap.title: chapter 13
beats: Baphomutt the imp starts haunting the castle, leaving stolen jewels in my room.
I try to get rid of him, but he’s too loyal (and too stupid) to leave.

roadmap.title: chapter 14
beats: My parents find the jewels.
I improvise a story about "finding them for the poor." They declare me a charitable prodigy and hold a festival in my honor.

roadmap.title: chapter 15
beats: The festival turns into a disaster when Baphomutt "helps" by stealing the royal crown.
I have to "find" it in the garden, pretending it’s a game.

roadmap.title: chapter 16
beats: Eris and I have a tea party while discussing soul transference.
She thinks it’s a "theoretical exercise." I let her believe it.

roadmap.title: chapter 17
beats: Leo challenges me to a horse race.
I try to sabotage his saddle, but he interprets it as "playful mischief" and declares me his "fierce rival."

roadmap.title: chapter 18
beats: Zephyr receives an anonymous note—a crayon drawing of a demonic horse.
He burns it, whispering, "Just a clever little girl."

roadmap.title: chapter 19
beats: I attempt to cast a light spell to read at night.
It backfires, singeing my eyebrows.
My mother prescribes "more rest."

roadmap.title: chapter 20
beats: The cult of the Eternal Flame kidnaps me, believing I’m the key to resurrecting Maledictus.
I correct their ritual syntax.
They weep with awe.

roadmap.title: chapter 21
beats: The cult’s ritual dagger drains my life force.
I’m furious—not because I’m in danger, but because they’re trying to sacrifice me to me.

roadmap.title: chapter 22
beats: Cornered, I utter the Word of Unmaking, dissolving the ritual circle.
My eyes flash dark.
The cultists flee, screaming about the Demon Lord’s return.

roadmap.title: chapter 23
beats: My parents burst in.
My mother examines the trace magic and declares I performed a miracle.
The cultists are arrested for blasphemy.

roadmap.title: chapter 24
beats: I collapse from the strain.
My father carries me to bed, telling me I’m his "little miracle." I realize I don’t want to leave.

roadmap.title: chapter 25
beats: Recovering, I ask for a pony—"a black one with red eyes." My father laughs and says, "Anything for my little miracle."

roadmap.title: chapter 26
beats: I start "infiltrating from within," deciding to be the best daughter in history.
My first act: organizing the royal library (and hiding forbidden books).

roadmap.title: chapter 27
beats: Leo visits again.
I try to poison his tea.
He drinks it and asks for seconds.

roadmap.title: chapter 28
beats: Eris presents me with a grimoire on soul transference.
I pretend to be excited.
She’s thrilled.

roadmap.title: chapter 29
beats: Zephyr receives another anonymous note—a perfect rune of command.
He shudders, then burns it.
"Just a clever little girl."

roadmap.title: chapter 30
beats: I attempt to cast a healing spell on a wounded sparrow.
It explodes.
The court assumes I’m "practicing."

roadmap.title: chapter 31
beats: My mother notices my "unusual" vocabulary during a piano recital.
I blame it on "too many books." She sighs and says, "More warm milk, then."

roadmap.title: chapter 32
beats: Baphomutt "helps" by stealing the royal cookie recipe.
The court assumes I’m "experimenting with flavors." I let them.

roadmap.title: chapter 33
beats: I try to teach Eris a forbidden spell.
She thinks it’s a game.
I let her believe it.

roadmap.title: chapter 34
beats: Leo challenges me to a duel.
I try to lose gracefully.
He interprets my "clumsiness" as "strategic brilliance" and declares me his equal.

roadmap.title: chapter 35
beats: Zephyr’s spies report that I’m "plotting something." I feed them false leads about a "jam conspiracy." He investigates the royal pantry.

roadmap.title: chapter 36
beats: I attempt to cast a sleep spell on my father.
It backfires, making me yawn.
He laughs and tucks me into bed.

roadmap.title: chapter 37
beats: The cult of the Eternal Flame sends a letter, begging for my blessing.
I ignore it.
My mother finds it and assumes it’s fan mail.

roadmap.title: chapter 38
beats: I try to summon a demonic gnat.
Nothing happens.
The court assumes I’m "meditating."

roadmap.title: chapter 39
beats: Leo confesses his "love" for me.
I glare at him.
He interprets it as "shyness." I give up and let him call me his "fierce little rose."

roadmap.title: chapter 40
beats: Eris and I have a tea party while discussing necromancy.
She thinks it’s "theoretical." I let her believe it.

roadmap.title: chapter 41
beats: Zephyr’s spies report that I’m "corrupting the youth." I feed them false leads about a "puppet conspiracy." He investigates the nursery.

roadmap.title: chapter 42
beats: I attempt to cast a fire spell.
It fizzles, singeing my sleeve.
My mother prescribes "more naps."

roadmap.title: chapter 43
beats: The cult of the Eternal Flame builds a shrine to me.
I ignore it.
My father finds it and assumes it’s a "charming garden ornament."

roadmap.title: chapter 44
beats: I ask for a black pony with red eyes.
My father laughs and says, "Anything for my little miracle." I smile.
The pony arrives the next day.

roadmap.title: chapter 45
beats: I ride my new pony through the royal gardens, Baphomutt perched on its back.
My parents wave from the balcony.
I wave back.
